understanding.emotion: heartbroken and unable to let go
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call not feeling good enough, and that is where this week begins.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the ache and the replaying, named without blame.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that grief is love with nowhere to go, and that is why the heart aches.
week_beats.steady: You hold that what is real in you cannot be taken, and both the love and the ending can be true.
week_beats.act: You try one act of letting the heart feel, and one act of turning away from the story.
week_beats.story: A woman who loved and was left shows you that grief is love with nowhere to go, and that you can survive it.

understanding.core_struggle: Her three-year relationship ended with a single text, and now she cannot stop watching his story and wondering if she is going mad.
understanding.mirror: Three years, one text, and now the story you cannot look away from.
understanding.insight: You are not going mad. You are grieving a real bond that ended by a text, and the mind will not let it rest until it is named.

situations.label: I can't let go of resentment
I have to give someone bad news
I've fallen out with my sibling
I feel guilty about something I did

queries.hook: The ache of a love that was real and has now ended, and the mind that will not stop replaying the moment it left.
queries.diagnose: Grief is love with nowhere to go; everything that comes together must part, and the heart aches because the bond was real.
queries.steady: What is real in you cannot be taken; the love was real, the ending was real, and both can be true at once.
queries.act: Let the heart feel what it feels, and let the mind rest; do not watch the story again today, and write down what the bond gave you.
queries.story: A woman who loved deeply and was left by a single text, who learned that grief is love with nowhere to go, and found her footing again.

weeks: Grief is love with nowhere to go

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verse.sanskrit: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
verse.line: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.
verse.translation: I see nothing that could drive away this sorrow that is drying up my senses, not even an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth or rule over the gods.
verse.why: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

prasang.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

verse.meaning: Arjuna is standing on the battlefield, his body shaking, his mouth dry. He has dropped his bow and arrow. He tells Krishna that even if he won every kingdom in the world or ruled over the gods, it would not touch the grief that is drying him up inside. He cannot see any way out of this sorrow. He admits he does not know what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
verse.for_you: You keep watching his story and replaying that last text. That ache is not madness. It is grief for a real bond that was cut off so cleanly. You are allowed to not know the way forward right now.
verse.try_today: Notice one thought that repeats and name it silently.
verse.scene_line: You are on a battlefield of your own, with your bow dropped and your senses dried up.
asks: How do I stop the mind from replaying his story?
What does it mean to ask for help when I feel this lost?
Can grief really dry up my senses like this?

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Vyasa
verse.setting: The sage Vyasa consoles Yudhishthira, who wants to starve himself to death in grief.
verse.sanskrit: संयोगा विप्रयोगाश्च जातानां प्राणिनां ध्रुवम् / बुद्धुदा इव तोयेषु भवन्ति न भवन्ति च
verse.line: Meeting and parting come to everyone. Like bubbles on water, they rise and they vanish.
verse.translation: For every living being, meeting and parting are certain. Like bubbles on water, they appear and are gone.
verse.why: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.

prasang.title: After the war: Yudhishthira's grief and his family's counsel
prasang.summary: Victorious but shattered by the deaths of kin, Yudhishthira wants to give up the throne for the forest. Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Nakula, the sage Devasthana and Vyasa each argue with him, about duty, guilt, grief and the shortness of life, until he agrees to rule.
prasang.story_hook: He had won the war, and all Yudhishthira wanted was to walk into the forest and never come back.
prasang.lesson: Guilt and grief are real, but they are not the end. The good you do next counts.

verse.for_you: A mistake is something you did, not who you are; no one who tries to do good is ever lost.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: Closing verse of the section on steadfastness.
verse.sanskrit: छिन्नोऽपि रोहति तरुश्चन्द्रः क्षीणोऽपि वर्धते लोके । इति विमृशन्तः सन्तः सन्तप्यन्ते न लोकेऽस्मिन् ॥
verse.line: A cut tree grows back; the waning moon fills again. Remembering this, the wise do not despair.
verse.translation: A tree that is cut grows again; the waning moon waxes again in the world. Reflecting on this, the good are not tormented in this world.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari closes his section on staying the course by reminding the reader that nature itself renews. A tree that has been cut down will grow again. The moon, even when it is almost gone, will wax again. This is the way of the world. If you hold this in mind, you will not let despair break you.
verse.for_you: You are staring at a phone screen waiting for a ghost. The grief is real, but the ending is also real. Your capacity to love was never broken. Hold onto the truth that you are still here, still whole, still able to grow back.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing in your room that is whole and unchanged.
verse.scene_line: You are the cut tree, and the ground is waiting.
asks: How do I know if I am grieving or just waiting?
What does it mean to grow back when I feel hollow?

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः । शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
verse.line: You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
verse.translation: This whole universe is pervaded by you and strung on you. By nature you are pure awareness; do not fall into smallness of mind.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free. Ashtavakra answers that this whole universe is strung on you. By nature you are pure awareness, so do not fall into smallness of mind.
verse.for_you: The text says you are pure awareness, wider than any worry. That means the part of you that loves and the part of you that is being left are both real. You are not just the person who was left by a text.
verse.try_today: Notice when your mind shrinks into smallness and name it as a passing thought.
verse.scene_line: You are the awareness that watches the story, not the story itself.
asks: How do I hold the truth that I am more than this pain?

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: The sage Vasishtha to Bharat, shattered by his father's death and Ram's exile.
verse.sanskrit: तात हृदयँ धीरजु धरहु करहु जो अवसर आजु। उठे भरत गुर बचन सुनि करन कहेउ सबु साजु ॥
verse.line: Keep courage in your heart, and do what today asks of you.
verse.translation: "Child, keep courage in your heart, and do what this moment asks of you today." Hearing his teacher, Bharat rose and had everything made ready.
verse.why: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

prasang.title: Bharat refuses the throne
prasang.summary: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.
prasang.story_hook: Everyone agreed the throne was his, and Bharat could not bring himself to sit on it.
prasang.lesson: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

verse.for_you: Bharat's heart was heavy, yet he rose. You are waiting for a message that will not come. The mind keeps watching the story, hoping for a sign. You can do what today asks of you. Let the heart feel the hurt, then turn away from the phone.
verse.try_today: Watch the story once, then put the phone face down.
asks: How do I face a silence that feels like a verdict?
Who am I if I am not the one who is chosen?

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after losing his kingdom, and she will not let him stay there. She tells him not to think less of himself, not to settle for little, and to stop fearing. She says to set his mind on what is truly good, to pull himself together, and to act. She does not promise him his kingdom back. She just says that staying small and defeated is a choice, and that a person must set their mind on something worthy and move forward.
verse.for_you: The story on your screen is the same one you keep opening. You are not going mad. Your mind is stuck in the old failure of the breakup.
verse.try_today: Turn off the story and let your heart feel the quiet.
verse.scene_line: You lie defeated on your phone, and someone must rouse you.
asks: How do I stop letting his story own my mind?
What does it mean to set my mind on something good?

story.title: Pingala's song: the night she stopped waiting
story.story_hook: Pingala sat awake listening for footsteps that never came, until she stopped listening.
story.summary: Pingala waited all night for a lover who never came. At last she saw that her peace depended on someone else's arrival, let the expectation go, and slept peacefully.
story.lesson: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.

anchor.speaker: Pingala (quoted by Bhishma)
anchor.setting: Pingala, left waiting all night by a lover who never came, finally lets go and finds peace.
anchor.sanskrit: सुखं निराशः स्वपिति नैराश्यं परमं सुखम् / आशामनाशां कृत्वा हि सुखं स्वपिति पिङ्गला
anchor.line: Pingala let go of her expectation and slept peacefully. Letting go of expectation is the greatest ease.
anchor.translation: The one free of expectation sleeps in peace; freedom from expectation is the highest happiness. Turning hope into no-hope, Pingala sleeps peacefully.
anchor.why: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.
anchor.misuse: This is about clinging to an outcome, not about giving up hope in life.

prasang.title: Pingala's song: the night she stopped waiting
prasang.summary: Pingala waited all night for a lover who never came. At last she saw that her peace depended on someone else's arrival, let the expectation go, and slept peacefully.
prasang.story_hook: Pingala sat awake listening for footsteps that never came, until she stopped listening.
prasang.lesson: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.

story.hook_title: Pingala waited all night for a man who never came
story.teaser: Pingala waited all night for a man who never came
story.for_you: Pingala waited for a man who never came. They left a single message, and now your peace waits on a reply that will not come. The mind spins, but the night is long. Let the waiting end. Sleep can be yours again.
asks: How do I sleep when my heart is awake?
